title: DB Health Tripwire has never executed a single check — bare tsx exits 127 every run

sha_binding.verified_source_note: Every measurement in this bundle was taken on this lane's branch, built from main tip b5ebdc23. The workflow_dispatch runs cited below executed pre-rebase commits of the identical working tree; the rebase onto b5ebdc23 and the db-health-checks.ts split changed module boundaries, not check logic, and the static suite was re-run after both. The authoritative binding is the squash SHA written post-merge by post-merge-lane-close.yml.

defect.claim: The DB Health Tripwire has never executed a single check since it was added.

root_causes.summary: The workflow invoked `tsx` by bare binary name. tsx is a workspace devDependency and is not on the runner's PATH inside a raw `run:` block, so the step exited 127 before Node started.
root_causes.evidence: runs 30616577637, 30597176319, 30573430796, 30546729826, 30525259668 — all failure, steps 1-6 green, step 7 'Run DB health checks' red

root_causes.summary: `import postgres from 'postgres'` named a package present in no package.json and with no pnpm-lock.yaml entry anywhere in the repository. Fixing (1) alone would have moved the failure from exit 127 to MODULE_NOT_FOUND exit 1.
root_causes.evidence: pre-fix `pnpm exec tsx scripts/ops/db-health-tripwire.ts` -> Error: Cannot find module 'postgres', exit 1; `grep -n postgres pnpm-lock.yaml` matched only @supabase/postgrest-js

root_causes.summary: Discovered by the first live run. A check that trips because a quantity never happened has no numeric measurement; requiring one made the execution gate reject a correct production finding.
root_causes.evidence: run 30628974075 — [tripwire:gate] FAIL — checks[2] (autovacuum_staleness) is tripped but carries no measured value

root_causes.summary: The Linear alert would never have been delivered: commentCreate takes the issue UUID, not the identifier, and the error was logged as a warning and swallowed.
root_causes.evidence: run 30628974075 — Linear comment failed with 'issue not found' for the tripwire's tracking issue identifier

defect.why_invisible: The job's only signal was a red badge, and a red badge is also what a genuine finding looks like. A monitor that had never worked was indistinguishable from a monitor that was working and unhappy.

unit_tests.note: Runs inside the required `verify` context via pnpm test -> pnpm test:ops. No package.json script list was modified.

db_client_boundary.note: The pure check logic was split into scripts/ops/db-health-checks.ts so no `pnpm test` entrypoint reaches a module that constructs a database client.

bare_binary_guard.regression_fixture: the pre-fix line `tsx scripts/ops/db-health-tripwire.ts` is reported by the same guard

read_only_enforcement.note: The value Postgres itself returned for SHOW transaction_read_only, inside the same transaction as the catalog reads. The execution gate fails unless it is 'on'.

runs.purpose: first live execution — proves the harness now starts and reaches the database
runs.note: The execution gate failed here on root cause 3 — a correct finding with no numeric measurement. This run is retained because it demonstrates the gate refusing a receipt it could not validate rather than passing it.

runs.purpose: NEGATIVE DEMONSTRATION — same commit and same measured value, threshold lowered by workflow_dispatch input only
runs.conclusion: The same measurement produced a different verdict when only the threshold moved. A run that merely started could not produce that difference. The lowered threshold is committed nowhere.
runs.alert_safety: Any override suppresses the Linear alert, so a demonstration can never be mistaken for a production finding.

runs.purpose: confirming run — all three outcomes separated correctly
runs.gate_output: [tripwire:gate] PASS — 12/13 checks executed (2 pass, 10 tripped, 1 not run)

measured_checks.subject: provider_offer_history
measured_checks.note: never analysed — observed, but the quantity does not exist

queries.purpose: read-only transaction assertion, recorded rather than claimed
measures Postgres' own report of the transaction's read-only mode
autovacuum_staleness check: vacuum/analyze timestamps and live/dead tuple counts for the 5 monitored hot tables
queries.sql: SELECT relname, last_vacuum, last_autovacuum, last_analyze, last_autoanalyze, n_dead_tup::text, n_live_tup::text, ROUND(n_dead_tup::numeric / NULLIF(n_live_tup + n_dead_tup, 0) * 100, 2)::text AS dead_tup_pct FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE relname = ANY($1) ORDER BY relname

queries.purpose: table_size check: relation and total (heap+toast+index) sizes for the 5 monitored hot tables
queries.sql: SELECT relname, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(relid)) AS table_size, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) AS total_size, pg_total_relation_size(relid)::text AS total_bytes FROM pg_stat_user_tables WHERE relname = ANY($1) ORDER BY relname

queries.purpose: toast_bloat check: TOAST-plus-index size as a percentage of total relation size for the 2 TOAST-monitored tables
queries.sql: SELECT relname, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(pg_class.oid)) AS heap_size, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid) - pg_relation_size(pg_class.oid)) AS toast_plus_index_size, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid)) AS total_size, ROUND((pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid) - pg_relation_size(pg_class.oid))::numeric / NULLIF(pg_total_relation_size(pg_class.oid), 0) * 100, 1)::text AS toast_pct FROM pg_class JOIN pg_namespace ON pg_namespace.oid = pg_class.relnamespace WHERE nspname = 'public' AND relname = ANY($1) ORDER BY relname

runtime_proof.queries_provenance: Literal SQL text is taken directly from scripts/ops/db-health-tripwire.ts at merge SHA 5aee608a5c7f30539bcb94ffb8e56e9c0f5ad1bd. All five statements were genuinely executed against production (aws-1-us-west-2.pooler.supabase.com) inside a single READ ONLY transaction in workflow run 30629392553 (artifact db-health-tripwire-receipt-30629392553-1, schema db-health-tripwire-receipt/v1), the same run whose per-table results are already recorded under runtime_proof.runs and runtime_proof.measured_checks above. This satisfies R1 with the tripwire's own execution, which is the live-DB evidence for this specific lane -- pnpm test:db (the generic outbox/settlement suite exercised in CI run 30631299241) proves a different, unrelated code path and does not itself contain queries about DB-health check subjects, so it was not used as the R1 source.

row_counts.note: n_live_tup/n_dead_tup are 0 on the partitioned parent relation itself; independent review (see verifier.findings, review-1) measured the true aggregate size across partition children at 7.92GB via a separate live query -- recorded honestly here rather than smoothed over.

runtime_proof.row_counts_provenance: n_live_tup/n_dead_tup for the 5 monitored hot tables, taken verbatim from the 'display' fields of run 30629392553's db-health-tripwire-receipt.json artifact (downloaded and parsed to produce this list), not invented or estimated. This is the only DB-health-tripwire-specific row-count evidence this lane produced; it is a receipt of a live production measurement, satisfying R2 for this T1 lane.

outcome_separation.claim: A harness error, a healthy database and a real finding are three distinct outcomes reported by three distinct workflow steps.

mapping.Run DB health checks red: harness_error — the checks could not run
mapping.Prove the checks executed red: the run produced no usable proof of execution
mapping.Report DB health verdict red: the checks ran and one tripped — the only DB-unhealthy outcome

findings_handed_on.summary: Production bloat and vacuum findings are real and currently true: system_runs 1287.33 MB against a 500 MB threshold, raw_payloads 693.73 MB and odds_snapshots 427.21 MB against 300 MB, TOAST ratios of 99%, and 905.71 hours (37.7 days) since the last ANALYZE on every hot table. This is the signature of the June 2026 write-path degradation.
findings_handed_on.scope: out of scope for this lane, which restores detection; merging turns the scheduled monitor red for this reason

findings_handed_on.summary: statement_timeout_rate cannot run against its current data source. GET {SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/rpc/get_logs?type=postgres returns HTTP 404 — the endpoint does not exist. Postgres logs are reachable only via the Supabase Management API, which needs a credential this job deliberately does not hold.
findings_handed_on.disposition: recorded as not_run with the 404 as its reason rather than contributing an invisible pass; repairing it would expand privilege

findings_handed_on.summary: The Linear alert destination does not resolve — the tripwire's tracking issue returns 'Entity not found: Issue' for the token this workflow holds. Lookup and error handling are now correct and the failure is recorded and annotated, but the destination needs a decision.
findings_handed_on.disposition: annotated as a warning, never a job failure — conflating 'could not notify' with 'the database is unhealthy' is what this lane undoes

findings_handed_on.summary: The `runtime` lane contract cannot express a dependency fix: .lane/lanes/runtime.yml allows package.json but not pnpm-lock.yaml. Under pnpm 10 with --frozen-lockfile the pair is indivisible, so no dependency-adding runtime lane can satisfy the contract as written. `Lane authority` is red on this PR for that reason (outside_allowed_paths: pnpm-lock.yaml).
findings_handed_on.disposition: Deliberately not fixed here. Lane authority is not a required context, and widening a lane's authority to make one's own lane pass is a governance change that belongs in its own lane, not a side effect of a runtime fix.

verifier.review_method: Independent adversarial review by a separate Opus 5 agent session with no continuity from the implementing session. The reviewer read the pre-fix and post-fix diffs directly from git history (git show 5aee608a and 5aee608a~1) and ran read-only SQL against production (zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm) to check the proof bundle's claims rather than trusting its narrative.
verifier.verdict_summary: The four core defect claims (bare-tsx exit 127, phantom postgres import, mechanically-enforced read-only transaction, removal of the fail-open exit(0) handler) were independently verified true against the actual diff and pre-fix code. The reviewer also found three real, previously-unflagged defects in the check logic that this lane inherited from the pre-fix script rather than introduced: (1) pg_total_relation_size(relid) returns 0 for the partitioned table provider_offer_history because partition children hold the actual bytes, so the table_size check false-negatives (reports PASS) on a table independently measured at 7.92GB via live production query -- the largest object in the database; (2) evaluateAutovacuumRow selects last_autoanalyze but never reads it, so the staleness measurement uses only last_analyze even when autoanalyze ran far more recently, overstating staleness; (3) missingVacuum alone forces severity:critical even under normal autovacuum-only maintenance (last_vacuum is always null in that mode), making the check permanently red by construction and reintroducing the 'red badge means nothing' ambiguity this lane exists to remove.

findings.summary: table_size check false-negatives on provider_offer_history: pg_total_relation_size(relid) on the partitioned parent returns 0 bytes because content lives in partition children, not the parent relation. Live query against canonical production (zfzdnfwdarxucxtaojxm) during review measured the table at 8,499,781,632 bytes (7.92 GB) across 60 partitions -- larger than the other four monitored tables combined -- while the tripwire reports 0 MB / PASS.
findings.disposition: not fixed in this closeout PR (evidence-bundle-only scope); inherited from the pre-fix script, not introduced by UTV2-1632; recorded here as a genuine finding for follow-up

findings.summary: evaluateAutovacuumRow (scripts/ops/db-health-checks.ts) selects last_autoanalyze in the query but never reads it when computing staleness, using only last_analyze. On review date, last_analyze was 2026-06-23 (the manual UTV2-1294 ANALYZE) for all five hot tables while last_autoanalyze was materially more recent (2026-06-30 through 2026-07-12) -- the 905.71-hour staleness figure is arithmetically correct for last_analyze alone but overstates how stale planner statistics actually are.
findings.disposition: not fixed in this closeout PR; inherited from the pre-fix script

findings.summary: missingVacuum (last_vacuum IS NULL) alone forces severity:critical in the autovacuum_staleness check, but last_vacuum is null under normal autovacuum-only maintenance with no manual VACUUM ever run -- meaning the check can never pass in steady state and the scheduled monitor is permanently red by construction, which is the same 'red badge is ambiguous' problem this lane's stated purpose is to eliminate.
findings.disposition: not fixed in this closeout PR; inherited from the pre-fix script; workflow-hardening.test.ts currently encodes this behavior as expected

verifier.findings_handed_on_note: These three findings are additive to, and do not contradict, the four core defect claims verified true above (bare-tsx exit 127, phantom postgres dependency, read-only transaction enforcement, fail-open removal). They concern the correctness of check logic this lane restored execution to, not whether it now executes.
